newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Schmidhuber-debate on soft euro "premature".
newsitem.headline: Buba's Schmidhuber-debate on soft euro "premature".

text.p: Bundesbank council member Peter Schmidhuber said on Wednesday the debate about softening entry criteria for European currency union or delaying the start was "premature and damaging."

"This debate cannot be held at any serious level at the moment...it is premature and damaging because it lessens efforts to consolidate and, at worst, can have the effect of a self-fulfilling prophecy," Schmidhuber said in text of a speech. Schmidhuber said the start of European economic and monetary union should not be hampered by political concessions, which he said could endanger the whole project.

"The start of EMU should not be hampered by political concessions. In that case, the whole project could be put in jeopardy. A bad start would shake trust in the common currency, not only in the EU, but also in international financial markets," Schmidhuber said.
He also said the view that a less stable euro would lead to increased employment was a fateful error.
"The opinion that one hears here and there, also in Germany, that one can have more jobs with less stability is a fateful error," Schmidhuber said.
